title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a police deployment. A licensed operator used camera and records systems, Flock, CJIS and CORI, for a purpose they were not provisioned for, tracking a person he had previously dated. The systems performed as designed: they returned location and record data to an authenticated officer. Nothing in the reported facts shows the software was deceived or that it failed technically.

The failure sits at the point where authorised access meets unauthorised purpose. Query tools of this kind are built to answer requests from people who already hold the credentials, so the misuse is invisible to the system itself and visible only in the pattern of who is being looked up and how often. Catching it would have required auditing query logs against the officer's own connections, or a tip from the person being searched, which is what appears to have happened here.

What is not established is whether Rogers is guilty of any offence. A criminal complaint is an allegation, an internal affairs finding is an administrative conclusion, and a pending hearing is not a ruling.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and opened an internal affairs investigation. After four weeks, the department found he had used state systems to obtain information about the woman and placed him on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing next week could decide Rogers' employment status.
